the landlord
may claim of the security only those amounts as are reasonably necessary for the purposes specified in subdivision (b).

details.requirement: Claims for materials, supplies, and work must be limited to a reasonable amount necessary to restore the premises to their inception-of-tenancy condition, excluding ordinary wear and tear.

shall be limited to a reasonable amount necessary to restore the premises back to the condition it was
in at the inception of the tenancy, exclusive of ordinary wear and tear.

details.requirement: Within a reasonable time after notice of intent to terminate or before the lease ends, the landlord must notify the tenant in writing of the option to request an initial inspection and the right to be present.
details.quote: the landlord shall notify the tenant in writing of the tenant’s option to request an initial inspection and of the tenant’s right to be present at the inspection.

details.quote: upon the request of the tenant, make an initial inspection of the premises prior to any final inspection the landlord makes after the tenant has vacated the premises.

details.key_value: At least 48 hours’ prior written notice.
details.quote: The landlord shall give at least 48 hours’ prior written notice of the date and time of the inspection

details.quote: The landlord shall proceed with the inspection whether the tenant is present or not, unless the tenant previously withdrew their request for the inspection.

details.requirement: Based on the inspection, the landlord must provide an itemized statement identifying proposed repairs or cleanings that may be deducted and include the specified statutory text; give it to the tenant if present or leave it inside the premises.
details.quote: the landlord shall give the tenant an itemized statement specifying repairs or cleanings that are proposed to be the basis of any deductions from the security

details.requirement: The tenant has an opportunity between the initial inspection and termination to remedy identified deficiencies consistently with the rental agreement, to avoid security deductions.
details.quote: The tenant shall have the opportunity during the period following the initial inspection until termination of the tenancy to remedy identified deficiencies

details.requirement: After a qualifying initial inspection, the landlord may not deduct for repairs or cleanings not identified in the itemized statement.
details.quote: the landlord shall not use the security for deductions for repairs or cleanings that are not identified in the itemized statement described in paragraph (2).

details.requirement: For tenancies beginning on or after July 1, 2025, the landlord must photograph the unit immediately before or at the inception of the tenancy.
details.quote:
the landlord shall take photographs of the unit immediately before, or at the
inception of, the tenancy.

details.quote: the landlord shall take photographs of the unit within a reasonable time after the possession of the unit is returned to the landlord, but prior to any repairs or cleanings for which the landlord will make a deduction from or claim against the security deposit pursuant to this section, and shall also take photographs of the unit within a reasonable time after such repairs or cleanings are completed.

details.quote: No later than 21 calendar days after the tenant has vacated the premises

details.quote: the landlord shall return the remainder of the security by personal delivery or by a check made payable to the tenant and mailed by first-class mail, postage prepaid.

the landlord shall return the remainder of the security electronically to a bank account or other financial
institution designated by the tenant in writing

details.quote: the landlord or the landlord’s successor in interest shall, within a reasonable time after notification of either party’s intention to terminate the tenancy, or before the end of the lease term, notify the tenant in writing of the tenant’s right to receive the security electronically

details.quote:
the landlord shall
furnish the itemized statement by personal delivery or first-class mail, postage prepaid.

the landlord may

A housing provider shall provide the information

A housing provider

tenant_conditions: A tenant in an owner-occupied two- or three-family dwelling may make the Security Deposit Law applicable by sending the landlord a written request and allowing 30 days.
key_value: 1.5 times one month’s rent

details.requirement: After a tenant terminates a lease under the Safe Housing Act, the landlord must make the security deposit and interest available to the tenant or the tenant’s agent within 15 business days after termination.
details.key_value: 15 business days after lease termination
details.quote:
Within 15 business days after the lease  is terminated, the landlord shall make available 
the return of the tenant’s security deposit, plus any interest earned, to the tenant or the tenant’s 
agent.

details.requirement: Within three business days after lease termination, the landlord must give the tenant written notice stating when and where the tenant can collect the security deposit.
details.key_value: 3 business days after lease termination
details.quote:
within three business days after the lease is terminated, the landlord must notify 
the tenant in writing of when and where the tenant can pick up the security deposit.

details.requirement: The landlord must keep the security deposit available for return during normal business hours for 30 days in the municipality where the rental property is located.
details.key_value: 30 days
details.quote:
The security deposit must be available for return 
during normal business hours for thirty (30) days in the municipality where the rental property is 
located.

details.requirement: The returned security deposit must be accompanied by an itemized list of interest earned and deductions.
details.quote:
The security deposit must be accompanied by an itemized list of the interest earned and 
any deductions.

details.requirement: If security money is not demanded and returned to the tenant or designated agent within 30 days, the landlord must redeposit or reinvest it in accordance with the Security Deposit law.
details.key_value: 30 days
details.quote:
Any security money not demanded by and returned to the tenant or th e tenant’s 
designated agent within 30 days shall be redeposited or reinvested by the landlord, in accordance 
with the Security Deposit law.

details.requirement: The landlord may charge the tenant for amounts due under the lease, including qualifying property damage and rent due when the lease terminates.
details.quote:
The landlord may charge the tenant for any money due the landlord 
under the terms of the lease, including damages to the property that are not ordinary wear and tear 
and any rent due and owing at the time the lease is terminated

details.requirement: When a service member properly terminates a lease under the Service Members Civil Relief Act, the landlord must return the security deposit in accordance with the applicable Security Deposit Law.
details.quote:
The landlord is required to return the security 
deposit in accordance with the applicable Security Deposit Law

details.requirement: A yearly increase in the security deposit may not exceed 10% of the current security deposit.
details.key_value: 10% of the current security deposit
details.quote:
Any additional 
yearly security deposit increase may not exceed 10% of the current security deposit.

details.requirement: A landlord may not charge a pet security deposit that causes the combined pet and regular security deposits to exceed one and one-half times one month’s rent.
details.key_value: 1.5 times one month’s rent, combined
details.quote:
A landlord 
may not charge a pet security deposit if it exceeds one and one-half times one month’s rent when 
combined with the regular security deposit.

details.requirement: Funds prepaid and held to secure future rent are treated as part of the security deposit, regardless of how they are labeled.
details.quote:
Therefore, any prepaid funds held to secure future rents are considered to be a part of the security 
deposit. This includes the last month’s rent. It does not matter how the prepaid funds are labeled.

details.requirement: At the inception of the lease, a landlord may require no more than one and one-half times monthly rent as security, plus the first month’s rent.
details.key_value: 2.5 times the monthly rent
details.quote:
The landlord may only require one and one -half times the tenant’s monthly rent as security and 
the first month’s rent at the inception of the lease. That means the landlo rd may not require more 
than two and one-half times the monthly rent at the inception of the lease

details.requirement: The recipient must hold the security deposit in trust, must not use it in a manner not permitted by law, must not commingle it with personal property, and must not make it an asset of the landlord.
details.quote:
The security deposit money continues to be the property of the person making the deposit 
and must be held in trust by the person receiving the money. This means that the person who 
receives the money must not use the money in any way not permitted by law.

details.requirement: For security deposits received for ten or fewer units, the landlord or designee must deposit the money in an insured New Jersey bank or savings and loan association in an interest-bearing account.
details.key_value: Insured, interest-bearing account at a New Jersey bank or savings and loan association
details.quote:
A landlord or designee who receives security deposit money for ten or less units must 
deposit that money in an insured bank or savings and loan association located in New Jersey in an 
interest-bearing account at the current interest rate at the time of deposit.

details.requirement: For security deposits received for ten or more units, the landlord or designee may invest in an insured money market fund of a New Jersey-based investment company with investments maturing in one year or less, or deposit the money in a State or federally chartered New Jersey bank or savings and loan association in an account bearing a variable rate of interest.
details.quote:
A landlord or designee 
who receives security deposit money for 10 or more units has the option of investing the money in 
an insured money market fund of a New Jersey-based investment company where the investments 
mature in one year or less, or deposit that money in a State or federally charted bank, or savings, 
and loan association located in New Jersey in an account bearing a variable rate of intere st.

details.requirement: Interest or earnings on the security deposit belong to the tenant and must be paid in cash or credited against rent due on the lease renewal or anniversary, or on January 31 if the tenant has received written notice that interest will be paid annually on that date.
details.quote:
The interest or earnings paid on the security deposit belongs to the tenant and shall be paid 
to the tenant in cash or credited toward rent due and owing on the ren ewal or anniversary of the 
tenant’s lease or on January 31,  if the tenant has been given written notice, that the interest 
payments will be paid on January 31 of each year

details.requirement: Within 30 days after receiving the deposit and at each annual interest payment, the landlord must give the tenant written notice of the financial institution or investment company, deposit amount, account type, and current interest rate.
details.key_value: Within 30 days of receipt and at each annual interest payment
details.quote:
Within 30 days of receipt of the security deposit and at t he time of each annual interest 
payment, the landlord must notify the tenant in writing of the name and address of the banking 
institution or investment company in which the money is deposited, the amount of the deposit, 
type of account, and current rate o f interest for the account.

details.requirement: The landlord must notify the tenant within 30 days after transferring the deposit to a new landlord or moving it to another account or bank.
details.key_value: Within 30 days
details.quote:
the landlord must notify 
the tenant within 30 days of transferring security deposit money to a new landlord or moving the 
security deposit to another account or bank.

details.requirement: If the landlord fails to give required notice or pay required interest, the tenant may, after giving written notice, apply the deposit and interest at 7% per year to rent due or to become due. For failure concerning annual notice or interest, the tenant must first allow the landlord 30 days to comply.
details.key_value: 7% per annum
details.quote:
If a tenant does not receive proper notice or is not paid 
interest as required, the tenant may use the security deposit for payment of rent by giving the 
landlord written notice that the security money plus interest at the rate of 7% per annum be applied 
to rent payments or payments due or to become due  from the tenant.

details.requirement: Within 30 days after termination of the tenancy, the landlord must return the security deposit plus interest earned, less permitted deductions.
details.key_value: Within 30 days after termination of tenancy
details.quote:
Within 30 days after the termination of a tenancy, a landlord must return the security 
deposit, plus interest earned less deductions

details.requirement: Deductions may include damage beyond normal wear and tear and other money due under the lease; no deductions may be made while the tenant remains in possession.
details.quote:
Deductions may 
include the cost of any damages over and above normal wear and tear, and any other money due 
the landlord under the terms of the lease.

details.requirement: If the landlord makes deductions from the deposit, the landlord must send the tenant an itemized list by registered or certified mail within 30 days after termination of the tenancy.
details.key_value: Within 30 days from termination of tenancy
details.quote:
If there are a ny deductions made from the security deposit 
by the landlord, an itemized list of these deductions must also be sent to the tenant by registered 
or certified mail within 30 days from the termination of the tenancy.

details.requirement: Within five business days after qualifying displacement by fire, flood, condemnation, or evacuation, the landlord must return the security deposit when a public official has prohibited occupancy or certified that displacement is expected to last longer than seven days.
details.key_value: Within five business days
details.quote:
Within five (5) business days after a tenant is displaced by fire, flood, condemnation, or 
evacuation, the landlord must return the security deposit. The law requires the return when either 
an authorized public official has posted a notice prohibiting occupancy or has certified that the 
displacement is expected to continue longer than seven (7) days.

details.requirement: Within three business days after receiving notice of the displacement, the landlord must tell the tenant where the security deposit can be collected.
details.key_value: Within three business days after receiving notice
details.quote:
Within three (3) business days of 
having received notice of the displacement, the landlord must let the tenant know where the 
security deposit can be collected.

details.requirement: When property is sold or transferred, the new owner must obtain the security deposit and accrued interest from the former owner and remains responsible for investment, notices, interest payments, and return of the deposit and earnings.
details.quote:
If the property is sold or transferred it is the duty of the new owner to obtain the security 
deposit, plus accrued interest on the tenant’s deposit, that was collected by the former owner.

details.requirement: A landlord who willfully and intentionally withholds a security deposit made by or for a tenant receiving State or federal financial assistance may be subject to a civil penalty of $500 to $2,000 for each offense.
details.key_value: $500 to $2,000 per offense
details.quote:
Any landlord who willfully and intentionally withholds a security deposit made by or on 
behalf of a tenant who has received financial assistance through any Stat e or federal program, 
including welfare or rental assistance , may be penalized. The landlord may be liable for a civil 
penalty of not less than $500 or not more than $2,000 for each offense.

details.requirement: When a tenant invokes constructive eviction and the landlord is found negligent in maintaining the rental unit, the tenant is entitled to return of the security deposit.
details.quote:
If a tenant invokes the remedy of constructive eviction, and 
the landlord is found to be negligent in maintaining the rental unit, the tenant is entitled t o the 
return of the security deposit

details.requirement: A landlord may not raise the rent during the lease term; the existing lease must be terminated and a new lease offered at the increased rent.
details.quote:
A landlord cannot raise the 
rent mid-lease term. The old lease must be terminated, and the new lease must have the increased 
rental payment.

details.requirement: To terminate the lease for a rent increase, the landlord must give proper written notice that the current lease is terminated and the tenant can remain by signing a new lease at the increased rent.
details.quote:
Landlord must give the tenant proper written notice, which informs the tenant that the current 
lease is terminated, and the tenant can remain in the premises by signing a new lease at an 
increased rent.

details.requirement: The written notice must state that when the current lease ends, the tenant has the right to continue renting the premises at the increased rent.
details.quote:
Written notice must also state that  end of the current lease, tenant has the right to continue 
renting the premises at the increased rent.

details.requirement: Before evicting a tenant for nonpayment of an increased rent, the owner must serve a valid notice to quit and a notice of rent increase.
details.quote:
before an owner can evict a tenant for nonpayment of 
an increased rent, they must first serve the tenant with a valid notice to quit and notice of rent 
increase.

details.requirement: A rent-increase notice does not itself require the tenant to leave; the tenant may remain by paying any legal increase in rent.
details.quote:
This notice does not mean that the tenant must actually leave; the tenant has the right to 
remain as long as they pay any legal increase in rent.

details.requirement: After conversion to condominium, cooperative, or fee-simple unit ownership, rents may not be increased to cover costs resulting solely from the conversion.
details.quote:
If a building is converted to a condominium or cooperative form of ownership, or to fee 
simple ownership of units, rents may not be increased to cover cos ts resulting solely from the 
conversion

details.requirement: A landlord must give qualifying senior citizens and benefit recipients five business days to pay rent due on the first of the month and may not assess delinquency or late charges during that period.
details.key_value: Five business days
details.quote:
Any senior citizen receiving a Social Security Old Page Pension, a Railroad Retirement 
Pension, or any other governmental pension in lieu of a Social Security Old Age Pension, and any 
recipients of Social Security Disability Benefits, Supplemental Security Income, or benefits under 
Work First New Jersey, must be given a period of five (5) business days grace period for payment 
when the rent is due on the first of the month. No delinquency or late charge may be assessed 
during the grace period.

details.requirement: Owners of eligible properties with five or more rental units may be required to pass the full amount of qualifying property tax reductions to tenants as a rent credit or cash rebate.
details.key_value: Full amount of the qualifying property tax reduction
details.quote:
may require owners of properties with five (5) or more rental units to 
pass on to their tenants as a rent credit or cash rebate, the full amount of any current property tax 
reduction.

details.requirement: Where a rebate is due, distribute it in monthly installments at rent payment dates, beginning within 30 days after receipt of the notice of tax reduction; complete rebates by December 31, or by June 30 of the following year if the notice is received after November 1.
details.quote:
Generally, rebates are to be distributed in monthly installments 
at rent payment dates, beginning within 30 days after receipt of Notice of Tax Reduction. The first 
rebate is to be cumulative from January and all are to be completed by December 31.

details.requirement: A landlord may seek eviction for failure to pay an increased rent only if the increase is not unconscionable and complies with other applicable laws and municipal ordinances, including rent control.
details.quote:
The rent increase must not be unconscionable and 
must comply with all other laws or municipal ordinances, including rent control.

details.requirement: A tenant who believes a rent increase is unconscionable may withhold the difference between the old rent and the increased rent; the landlord may still sue and the court determines whether the increase is unconscionable.
details.quote:
If the tenant believes the rent increase is unconscionable, they may withhold a 
portion of the rent. They may withhold the difference between the old rent rate and the 
new increased rate.

details.requirement: A landlord may not refuse to renew a residential lease without good cause, except for the stated excluded housing.
details.quote:
No landlord of residential rental properties except t hose in owner occupied two or three 
family dwellings, motels or hotels, transient, or seasonal units may fail to renew any lease, 
regardless of whether it is written or oral unless they have good cause not to renew the lease.

details.requirement: Give the registration statement in writing to each tenant and post it in a readily visible place in the building. The statement must contain the information specified by law.
details.quote:
The registration statement must be given in writing to each tenant and posted in a place in 
the building where it can be easily seen.

details.requirement: File an amended registration with the correct agency within 20 days after any change to the information on the certificate.
details.key_value: Within 20 days after a change
details.quote:
Every landlord required to file a certificate of registration must file an amended registration 
with the correct agency (Bureau of Housing Inspection or clerk of the municipality) within 20 days 
after any changes to the information on the certificate.

details.requirement: Post amended registration statements in the building and notify each tenant in writing within seven days after filing the amended statement.
details.key_value: Within seven days after filing
details.quote:
Amended 
registration statements must also be posted in the building and each tenant must be notified in 
writing within seven (7) days after filing the amended statement.

details.requirement: A landlord may not evict a tenant in the building if the landlord has not been properly registered.
details.quote:
The landlord 
registration law prohibits a landlord from evicting a tenant in the building if the landlord has not 
been properly registered

details.requirement: A residential landlord may not evict a tenant or fail to renew a lease without good cause, and must be able to prove the grounds in court.
details.quote:
No residential landlord may evict or fail to renew a 
lease, whether it is a written or an oral lease without good cause. The landlord must be able to 
prove in court that he has grounds for an eviction.

details.requirement: A landlord may recover possession only by tenant consent or through legal eviction proceedings; a judgment for possession must be entered before the tenant is required to move.
details.quote:
A landlord may recover possession of a dwelling unit used as a residence only by 
consent of the tenants or through the legal process of eviction.

details.requirement: A landlord must serve a notice to quit for good-cause evictions, except for nonpayment of rent; each cause other than nonpayment must be described in detail in written notice.
details.quote:
Each cause, except for nonpayment of rent, must be described in detail by the landlord 
in a written notice to the tenant. A “Notice to Quit” is required for all good cause evictions, 
except for an eviction for nonpayment of rent

details.requirement: A landlord must give a 14-day notice before filing an eviction suit for nonpayment of rent when the tenant resides in federally subsidized housing.
details.key_value: 14 days
details.quote:
I f the tenant 
resides in federally subsidized housing a 14-day notice must be given before filing a suite 
for eviction

details.requirement: When a notice to cease is required, the time allowed for the tenant to comply must be reasonable under the circumstances.
details.quote:
There is no statutory time period for a “Notice to Cease,” however, the period of time for 
a resident to comply with the notice must be reasonable under the circumstances

details.requirement: A warrant for possession may not be issued until three business days after judgment for possession is granted.
details.key_value: 3 business days
details.quote:
The warrant for possession may not be issued unt il three (3) business 
days after the judgment for possession is granted.

details.requirement: The landlord must apply for a warrant for possession within 30 days after judgment for possession, unless the judgment is vacated through a court order or other written agreement signed by the landlord and tenant.
details.key_value: 30 days
details.quote:
A landlord must apply for a warrant for possession within 30 days from the date of 
the judgment for possession unless the judgment is vacated through a court order or other  written 
agreement signed by the landlord and tenant.

details.requirement: A landlord may not evict or lock out a tenant without consent or a court judgment; only a court officer may physically evict a tenant after a judge issues a warrant for removal.
details.quote:
“Self-help” eviction is entry into a dwelling unit and removal of tenants without their 
consent or without a judgment from a court, are  not permitted in New Jersey under any 
circumstances.

details.requirement: A landlord or agent may not padlock the premises, disconnect utilities, or otherwise block entry while the tenant still lives there.
details.quote:
A landlord or their agent may not padlock, disconnect utilities or otherwise block entry to 
a rental premise while the tenant still lives there.

details.requirement: Following eviction, a landlord must allow the tenant to remove personal belongings; belongings may only be removed in accordance with the Abandoned Property Law.
details.quote:
Following the eviction, the landlord must allow the tenant to remove their personal 
belongings from the premises. A landlord cannot keep the tenant’s belongings but can arrange for 
their storage.

details.requirement: For evictions under the stated health, safety, or removal-from-market grounds, relocation assistance must be provided before the tenant can be evicted.
details.quote: The tenant can’t be evicted until relocation assistance is provided.

details.requirement: For an eviction under subsection G(3), the landlord must pay relocation assistance equal to six times the tenant’s monthly rent.
details.key_value: six times the tenant’s monthly rent
details.quote:
Any tenant evicted under G 3) (illegal occupancy) is entitled to relocation assistance in 
an amount equal to six times the tenant’s monthly rent. The landlord is responsible f or 
paying the tenant’s relocation expenses.

details.requirement: For an illegal-occupancy eviction, the landlord must pay relocation assistance at least five days before removal; where the landlord does not pay on time, the municipality may pay from its revolving fund if it has one.
details.key_value: at least five days before removal
details.quote:
Any tenant who does not receive the required 
payment from the landlord at least five days prior to their removal f rom the premises, 
may receive payment from a revolving relocation assistance fund established by t he 
municipality.

details.requirement: If no municipal relocation assistance fund exists and the landlord fails to pay required relocation funds on time, interest accrues at 18% per year until payment in full, and the amount due is a lien on the property.
details.key_value: 18% per year
details.quote:
However, if the municipality has not established a relocation assistance fund, and the 
landlord does not pay the relocation funds within the required time, interest will accrue 
on the unpaid balance at the rate of 18% per year until the amount due, includi ng 
interest is paid in full to the tenant.

details.requirement: For an eviction to permanently retire a building or mobile home park from residential use under subsection H, the landlord must serve a notice to quit at least 18 months before filing suit; legal action may not begin until the lease expires.
details.key_value: 18 months
details.quote:
A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least 18 months 
prior to filing the suit for eviction. No legal action may be taken until the lease expires

details.requirement: For a specified conversion to condominium, cooperative, or fee simple ownership, the landlord must serve a notice to quit at least three years before filing suit; legal action may not begin until the lease expires.
details.key_value: 3 years
details.quote:
A Notice to Quit must be ser ved on the tenant at least 
three years before filing a suit for eviction. No legal action may be taken until the lease 
expires

details.requirement: For the described post-conversion sale and personal-occupancy eviction, the landlord must give the tenant a statement that the property is being converted, serve a notice to quit at least two months before suit, and wait until the lease expires before taking legal action.
details.key_value: 2 months
details.quote:
A 
Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least two months prior to filing suit for 
eviction. No legal action may be taken until the lease expires.

details.requirement: An owner of three or fewer condominium or cooperative units seeking personal occupancy or a sale to a buyer seeking personal occupancy must serve notice to quit at least two months before filing suit and wait until the lease expires.
details.key_value: 2 months
details.quote:
A 
Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least two months prior to filing suit for 
eviction. No legal action may be taken until the lease expires.

details.requirement: When the tenant has not been offered a reasonable opportunity to examine and rent comparable housing, the court grants up to five one-year stays; if the landlord provides five months' free rent as relocation hardship compensation, no more than a one-year stay may be granted.

A tenant may ask the court for permission to remain due to special circumstances; if granted, the stay may not exceed one year unless landlord and tenant agree to an extension, and ordinarily all rent due must be paid.
details.key_value: one year
details.quote:
A tenant may ask the court for permission to stay in the premises due to special 
circumstances that moving may cause. This action is a stay of eviction.

details.requirement: A landlord may remove a tenant from an owner-occupied two- or three-family dwelling only by court order and upon proving one of the listed causes.
details.quote:
Tenants of landlord-occupied two- and three-family dwellings can be removed only when 
a court issues an order for eviction. However, in these cases, the landlord must prove that the tenant 
(a) is staying after the expiration of the term of the lease, (b) is staying after a failure to pay rent,

details.provision: Evictions for Owner-Occupied Two-and Three-Family Dwellings

details.provision: Evictions for Owner-Occupied Two-and Three-Family Dwellings
details.requirement: For eviction based on remaining after the lease expires, the landlord must give written notice for delivery of possession and the applicable notice to quit.
details.quote:
a tenant residing 
in an owner- occupied two- or three-family dwelling may be evicted if the landlord can show that 
the tenant is staying after the expiration of the lease and the landlord has given the tenant a written 
notice for delivery of possession of the property.

details.requirement: Owners of rooming and boarding houses must follow the good-cause and notice requirements of the Eviction Law when evicting residents, unless the Bureau orders otherwise.

require owners of rooming and boarding houses to follow the good causes and notice requirements 
of the Eviction Law when evicting residents, except if otherwise ordered by the Bureau

the owner give at least three (3) working days’ 
notice to the County Welfare Board before starting the eviction action for any resident

details.requirement: After receiving a notice of termination of tenancy, a public housing tenant may request a hearing from the housing authority.
details.quote:
In the case of an eviction, a public housing tenant may request a 
hearing from the housing authority after receiving a notice of termination of tenancy.

details.requirement: A housing authority may not begin an eviction action until the hearing decision has been mailed or delivered to the tenant and a notice to vacate has been served.

A housing 
authority may not begin an eviction action in court until t he decision of the hearing officer or the 
hearing panel has been mailed or delivered to the tenant and a notice to vacate has been served.

details.requirement: A landlord may not retaliate by eviction, substantial lease alteration, or refusal to renew when a tenant exercises specified civil rights.

details.requirement: A landlord may not evict a residential tenant solely because of foreclosure.
details.quote: Foreclosure alone is not grounds for eviction in New Jersey.

details.requirement: A buyer who wants to occupy a foreclosed property as a primary residence must provide a 90-day notice to quit before evicting the tenant.
details.key_value: 90 days
details.quote:
Before a tenant can be evicted due 
to foreclosure, the landlord must provide the tenant with a 90 -day notice to qui t when the 
foreclosed property has been purchased by a buyer who wants to personally occupy it as his or her 
primary residence.

details.requirement: A person acquiring a foreclosed property with residential rental units must notify tenants in English and Spanish within 10 business days after the sale that ownership has changed and they need not move because of foreclosure.
details.key_value: Within 10 business days after the sale
details.quote:
Any person acquiring a foreclosed property containing one or more residential rental units 
must provide notices to the tenants in English and Spanish, within 10 business days after the sale,

details.requirement: For buildings with 10 or fewer dwelling units, the new owner must make a good-faith effort to obtain tenant names, address notices to tenants by name unless unable to identify them, post the notice on each unit's front door, and send it by certified and regular mail.
details.quote:
In buildings with 10 or fewer dwelling units, the new owner 
must make a good faith effort to obtain the names of all the tenants occupying the property.  
Notices must be addressed to tenants by name, unless the new owner is unable to identify the tenant 
by name, then the owner shall address the notice to “Tenant.”  The notice must also be placed on 
the front door of each tenant’s unit and sent to each tenant via certified and regular mail

details.requirement: For a residential property with more than 10 dwelling units, the new owner must conspicuously display the tenant notice in a prominent common area, or, if there is no common area, in a conspicuous location in each building.
details.quote:
In a residential property containing more than 10 dwelling units, the new owner must 
provide notice to tenants occupying the property by conspicuously displaying a copy of the 
“NOTICE TO TENANTS” in a prominent location, such as a common area of the building or other 
structure on the property.

details.provision: Notice Requirements to Tenants Prior to the Transfer of Title Due to a Foreclosure Action
details.requirement: A foreclosing creditor must give tenants the prescribed notice of their rights during foreclosure with any written or verbal communication, including a request that they vacate before foreclosure or sale.
details.quote:
Any written or verbal communication, including a summons and complaint, an initial 
written or verbal communication by a foreclosing creditor, or any communication written or verbal 
that requests a tenant to vacate the property before the foreclosure or sale of the property, requires 
the foreclosing creditor to give notice to the tenants

details.provision: Notice Requirements to Tenants After the Transfer of Title Due to a Foreclosure Action
details.requirement: When making a bona fide monetary offer to induce tenants to move, the new owner must provide the required tenant notice with both the initial and final offer.
details.quote:
When making a bona fide monetary offer to induce tena nts to move, the new owner must 
provide a separate and different notice from the notice required to be given by a foreclosing 
creditor.  The new owner must provide a copy of the “NOTICE TO TENANTS” and give it with 
the initial and final written or verbal offer to the tenant.

details.provision: Notice Requirements to Tenants After the Transfer of Title Due to a Foreclosure Action
details.requirement: Acceptance of a bona fide monetary offer must be in writing and acknowledge the receipt date and the tenant's five-day review period.
details.key_value: Five-day review period
details.quote:
An acceptance of the offer by the t enant must be in writing and include an 
acknowledgement of the date of the receipt of the offer, and an understanding that the tenant had 
a five-day review period to accept or reject the offer presented.

details.provision: Notice Requirements to Tenants After the Transfer of Title Due to a Foreclosure Action
details.requirement: A tenant's acceptance of a bona fide monetary offer is voluntary, and no one may pressure the tenant to accept it.
details.quote:
the accepta nce of a bona fide monetary offer is 
voluntary.  The tenant shall not be pressured by anyone, including the person making the offer to 
accept any offer to vacate the property.

details.provision: Senior Citizens and Disabled Protected Tenancy
details.requirement: Qualified tenants in a building being converted to condominium, cooperative, or fee-simple unit ownership may be protected from eviction for 40 years if their family income meets the statutory threshold.
details.key_value: 40 years
details.quote:
Tenants may be protected from eviction for 40 years 
if their family income is not more than three (3) times the average per person income in their 
county or $50,000.00, whichever  is greater

details.provision: Senior Citizens and Disabled Protected Tenancy
details.requirement: The landlord or converter must notify all tenants of their right to file for protected tenancy if they may be eligible.

The landlord or converter is required to 
notify all tenants of their right to file for protected tenancy if they may be eligible.

details.quote:
Every landlord of a senior citizen housing project and every landlord of a unit within a

No discriminatory advertising  of any kind relating

A landlord may not charge a tenant with a disability

tenant_conditions: The no-fault grounds include owner/family occupancy, withdrawal from the rental market, specified government or court orders, and demolition or substantial remodel, subject to the statute’s stated requirements and limits.
A tenant’s lease terms and conduct may determine whether an at-fault ground applies; these are not building facts.

details.requirement: If the intended occupant does not move in within 90 days or does not occupy the property for at least 12 continuous months, the owner must offer the unit back to the displaced tenant at the prior rent and lease terms and reimburse specified moving expenses.
details.quote:
If the intended occupant does not occupy the residential rental 
property within 90 days after the tenant vacates or does not 
occupy the residential rental property for at least 12 
continuous months, the owner shall offer the residential rental 
property to the tenant who vacated it at the same rent and lease 
terms in effect at the time the tenant vacated and shall 
reimburse the tenant for reasonable moving expenses incurred 
in excess of any relocation assistance that was paid to the 
tenant in connection with the written notice terminating the 
tenancy.

details.requirement: The termination notice must include the prescribed statement that, if the substantial remodel or demolition is not commenced or completed, the landlord must offer the tenant an opportunity to re-rent on the same terms and prior rental rate.
details.quote:
If the substantial remodel of your unit or demolition of 
the property as described in this notice of termination is 
not commenced or completed, the landlord must offer 
you the opportunity to re-rent your unit with a rental 
agreement containing the same terms as your most 
recent rental agreement with the landlord at the rental 
rate that was in effect at the time you vacated.

details.requirement: If permits are required, the landlord must post a copy of the permit application at the property within three business days after submitting it.
details.key_value: Within three business days of permit-application submission
details.quote:
post at the residential rental property a copy of the 
application for the necessary permits within three 
business days of submittal of the application

details.requirement: If permits are required, the landlord must secure the necessary permits before issuing the written termination notice.
details.quote:
secure permits necessary for the demolition or 
substantial remodel of the residential rental property 
prior to issuing the written notice required in section 
98.0704(b)(4)(D).

details.requirement: The landlord must provide the specified written tenant-protection notice in at least 12-point font and in a manner complying with California Civil Code § 1632.
details.key_value: At least 12-point font
details.quote:
A landlord of residential rental property subject to this Division shall provide 
written notice in no less than 12-point font to the tenant, and in a manner that 
complies with California Civil Code section 1632, as may be amended

details.requirement: The landlord must include a copy of the Tenant Protection Guide with the written notice required by § 98.0705(a).
details.quote:
A landlord of residential rental property subject to this Division shall include 
a copy of the Tenant Protection Guide with the written notice required by 
section 98.0705(a).

details.requirement: For a covered tenancy existing before June 24, 2023, the landlord must provide the notice and Tenant Protection Guide directly to the tenant or as a lease addendum within 90 days of that date.
details.key_value: Within 90 days of June 24, 2023
details.quote:
the notice required by section 98.0705(a) and the 
Tenant Protection Guide required by section 98.0705(b) shall be provided to 
the tenant directly or as an addendum to the lease within 90 days of June 24, 
2023.

details.requirement: For covered tenancies commencing or renewed on or after June 24, 2023, the landlord must include the notice and guide in the lease, or provide a tenant-signed written notice at lease signing, and give the tenant a copy.
details.quote:
the notice required by 
section 98.0705(a) and the Tenant Protection Guide required by 
section 98.0705(b) shall be included in the lease, or as a written notice signed 
by the tenant at the time the lease is signed, with a copy provided to the 
tenant.

details.requirement: Before terminating for a curable lease violation, the landlord must give written notice describing the violation and an opportunity to cure under California Code of Civil Procedure § 1161(3).
details.quote:
Before a landlord issues a notice to terminate a 
tenancy for at-fault just cause that is a curable lease violation, the 
landlord shall first give written notice of the violation including a 
description of the violation and an opportunity to cure the violation 
under California Code of Civil Procedure section 1161(3), as may be 
amended.

details.requirement: For a no-fault termination, the landlord must give written notice at least 30 or 60 days before the proposed termination date, as required by California Civil Code § 1946.1, in at least 12-point font.
details.key_value: At least 30 or 60 days before termination; at least 12-point font
details.quote:
The landlord shall give written notice to the tenant 
at least 30 or 60 days prior to the proposed date of termination as 
required by California Civil Code section 1946.1, as may be amended, 
in no less than 12-point font.

details.requirement: The no-fault termination notice must describe the basis for termination.
details.quote:
The landlord shall provide a description of the basis for the 
termination.

details.requirement: The notice must state the tenant's right to relocation assistance by direct payment or rent waiver.
details.quote:
The notice shall state the tenant’s right to relocation assistance 
established in section 98.0706(c) by a direct payment to the 
tenant or rent waiver.

details.requirement: If the landlord elects direct payment, the notice must state the amount available and that payment will be made within 15 days of the notice.
details.key_value: Within 15 days from the notice
details.quote:
If the landlord elects to provide relocation assistance by 
a direct payment to the tenant, the notice shall state the 
amount of relocation assistance available to the tenant 
and that the landlord shall provide the payment within 
15 days from the date of the notice.

details.requirement: If the landlord elects rent waiver, the notice must state the amount waived and that no rent is due for the corresponding final months of the tenancy.
details.quote:
If the landlord elects to provide relocation assistance by 
rent waiver, the notice shall state the amount of rent 
waived and that no rent is due for the final 
corresponding months of the tenancy.

details.requirement: The notice must state the tenant's right to an offer to renew, the 30-day acceptance period, the five-year offer period, and the tenant's notification and address requirements.
details.key_value: 30 days to accept; offer right applies if re-rented within five years
details.quote:
The notice shall state the tenant’s right to receive an offer to 
renew the tenancy established in section 98.0706(d) and 
30 days to accept the offer in the event the residential rental 
property is offered again for rent or lease for residential 
purposes within five years of the date the tenant was evicted 
under sections 98.0704(b)(1), (3), or (4)

details.requirement: For a no-fault termination, the landlord must provide relocation assistance, regardless of tenant income or tenancy length, by direct payment or rent waiver at the landlord's option. Unless the senior/disabled amount applies, the direct payment equals two months of actual rent under the lease in effect on the notice date.
details.key_value: Two months of actual rent under the lease in effect on the date of notice
details.quote:
Unless section 98.0706(c)(1)(A)(ii) applies, the direct 
payment to the tenant shall be in an amount equal to 
two months of actual rent under the tenant’s lease in 
effect at the date of the notice.

details.requirement: As the alternative to direct payment, the landlord must waive and not collect rent currently due or becoming due through the end of the tenancy up to the applicable direct-payment amount.
details.key_value: Rent waived up to the applicable direct-payment amount
details.quote:
The landlord shall waive, and not collect the payment by 
tenant, of any currently due or future rent under the tenant’s 
lease at the time of the notice and through the remainder of the 
tenancy in an amount equal to the applicable direct payment as 
set forth in section 98.0706(c)(1)(A).

details.requirement: When multiple tenants occupy the property and the landlord elects direct payment, the landlord may make one payment to all tenants named in the lease.
details.quote:
When more than one tenant occupies the residential rental property 
and the landlord elects to provide direct payment of relocation 
assistance to the tenants, the landlord may make a single direct 
payment to all the tenants named in the lease.

details.requirement: Providing relocation assistance does not discharge the landlord's obligation to return deposits or security amounts owed to the tenant.
details.quote:
The relocation assistance required by this Division shall not relieve the 
landlord’s obligation to, and shall be in addition to, the return of any 
deposit or security amounts owed to the tenant.

details.requirement: Relocation assistance required by the Division must be credited against relocation assistance required by federal, state, or other local law.
details.quote:
Any relocation assistance required by this Division shall be credited 
against any other relocation assistance required by any federal, state, 
or other local law.

details.requirement: If the tenant does not vacate after the termination notice expires, the landlord may recover the actual relocation assistance paid as damages in an action to recover possession.
details.key_value: Actual amount of relocation assistance provided
details.quote:
If a tenant fails to vacate after the expiration of the notice to terminate 
the tenancy, the actual amount of any relocation assistance provided 
under this Division may be recoverable by landlord as damages in an 
action to recover possession of the residential rental property.

details.requirement: If the property is offered for residential rent or lease within five years after a qualifying no-fault eviction, the landlord must first offer it in writing to the displaced tenant, if the tenant timely requested an offer and provided an address. The tenant has 30 days after receipt to accept.
details.key_value: Five-year offer period; 30 days to accept

purposes within five years of the date the tenant was evicted under

residential rental property in writing to the tenant displaced from that unit by 
the no-fault just cause termination

The notice shall state the tenant’s right to receive an offer to

tenancy and at the landlord’s option, provide relocation assistance to 
the tenant by one of the following:

details.requirement: A landlord's failure to strictly comply with § 98.0706 renders any termination notice required by that section void.
details.quote:
a landlord's failure to strictly comply with section 98.0706 shall

Prior to making a buyout offer, the landlord 
shall provide each tenant in a residential rental property a written disclosure

details.quote:
The landlord shall provide each tenant a fully executed copy of the disclosure 
form within three days of its execution and retain a copy of each signed 
disclosure form for five years

details.requirement: A buyout agreement must be in writing.
details.quote: The buyout agreement shall be in writing.

details.requirement: The landlord must give each tenant a copy of the buyout agreement when the tenant signs it.
details.quote:
A copy of the buyout agreement shall be given to each tenant at the 
time the tenant signs the buyout agreement.

details.requirement: The agreement must include, in bold letters of at least 14-point font near the tenant signature space, statements that the tenant may refuse the agreement, that an agreement below applicable relocation assistance is unlawful and void, and that the tenant may consult an attorney.
details.key_value: bold, at least 14-point font

details.requirement: If the tenant primarily negotiates the buyout agreement or lease in a non-English language, orally or in writing, the landlord must provide English and translated versions of the agreement at the same time.
details.quote:
If the tenant primarily negotiates the buyout agreement or lease, orally 
or in writing, in a non-English language, the landlord shall provide the 
tenant with an English and a translated version of the buyout 
agreement at the same time.

details.requirement: A buyout agreement must provide an amount greater than the relocation assistance available to the tenant. An agreement for less than relocation assistance owed is void.
details.key_value: greater than the tenant's applicable relocation assistance
details.quote:
Buyout agreements must be for an amount that is 
greater than the amount of relocation assistance available to the tenant in 
section 98.0706(c).

details.requirement: The provisions of § 98.0707 may not be waived by buyout agreement. Any agreement term purporting to waive or limit tenant rights under that section is unenforceable and void.
details.quote:
The provisions of section 98.0707 may not be waived by a buyout 
agreement.

details.requirement: A landlord must not retaliate against a tenant for exercising a right provided by the Division or seeking its enforcement.

A landlord shall not retaliate against a tenant for exercising any right provided by 
this Division or seeking the enforcement of this Division.

details.requirement: A tenant claiming a violation of the Division may file an action against the landlord in a court of competent jurisdiction.

A tenant claiming a violation of this Division may file an action against a 
landlord in a court of competent jurisdiction.

details.requirement: In a civil action for a Division violation, a tenant may seek injunctive relief, equitable relief, and money damages, including punitive damages.
details.quote:
A tenant may seek injunctive relief, equitable relief, and money damages, 
including punitive damages, in a civil action against a landlord for a violation 
of this Division.

details.requirement: A tenant may raise any violation or noncompliance with the Division as an affirmative defense in an action by a landlord to recover possession.
details.quote:
A tenant may raise, as an affirmative defense, any violation or noncompliance 
with this Division in any action by a landlord to recover possession of a 
residential rental property.

details.requirement: A landlord who attempts to recover possession, or actually recovers possession, in violation of the Division is liable to the tenant in a civil wrongful-eviction action for damages of at least three times actual economic damages.

details.quote: The landlord shall rebate to the tenant any amount of rent collected in excess of that permissible pursuant to the terms of this chapter by crediting the tenant with the amount of excess rent paid over a period not to exceed fourteen (14) months, or in the event the tenant is no longer in occupancy, by refunding within a one (1) month period.

details.requirement: A tax surcharge may not exceed the formula-based amount: one-twelfth of the annual municipal property-tax increase divided by the total monthly rent roll, multiplied by the tenant's monthly rent. details.key_value: One-twelfth of annual property-tax increase divided by total monthly rent roll, multiplied by tenant's monthly rent; tenant share cannot exceed tenant's rent-roll percentage
details.quote: The landlord shall divide one-twelfth (1/12th) of the annual increase in the present property tax over the property tax of the previous year by the total monthly rent roll, and that product shall be multiplied by the monthly rent paid by each tenant to establish the amount of surcharge that each tenant shall be required to pay. The tenant shall not be liable for a tax surcharge exceeding the tenant's percentage of the entire rent roll for the dwelling.

details.requirement: A landlord seeking a tax surcharge must petition the Board and give the tenant and Board at least 30 days' advance notice of the calculation details listed in the ordinance.
details.key_value: At least 30 days before the proposed increase
details.quote: Any landlord seeking a surcharge shall petition the Board for approval and shall give notice to the tenant and the Board, at least thirty (30) days prior to the increase sought, of the calculations involved in computing the tax surcharge, including the present property tax for the dwelling; the property tax for the dwelling for the previous year; total rent rolls of all units, occupied or unoccupied in the dwelling

details.requirement: The tenant pays the tax surcharge in equal monthly payments only after the landlord gives one month's prior notice of the increase as required by statute.

details.quote: The tax surcharge each tenant is liable for shall be paid in equal monthly payments only after the landlord gives the tenant one (1) month prior notice of the increase as required by statute.

details.requirement: If municipal property taxes decrease because of a lower tax rate or assessed valuation, tenants are entitled to a tax decrease apportioned in the same manner as a tax surcharge.

details.quote: If the municipal property taxes are decreased in a given year due to either a decrease in the property tax rate or a lowering of the assessed evaluation of the property by the municipality, then the tenants are entitled to a tax decrease. details.requirement: When a landlord successfully appeals and obtains a tax reduction, the tenant must receive 75% of the reduction applicable to the tenant's tax portion, after reasonable appeal expenses are deducted.

details.quote: In the event a tax appeal is taken by the landlord and the landlord is successful in the appeal and the taxes reduced, the tenant shall receive seventy-five (75%) percent of the reductions as applied to its tax portion, after deducting all reasonable expenses incurred by the landlord in prosecuting the appeal.

details.requirement: After a successful tax appeal, the landlord must notify tenants within 30 days after receiving the rebate, provide the amount and calculations due to each tenant, and forward the amount due within that same 30-day period. details.key_value: Tenant notice within 14 days of notice of success; landlord notice and payment within 30 days of receiving the rebate
details.quote: The tenant must receive notice within fourteen (14) days from when the landlord receives his/her notice of successful appeal. details.requirement: For a major new improvement surcharge, the landlord must calculate average annual cost by dividing completed improvement cost by useful life, which cannot be less than one year; subtract annual cost savings; establish useful life; and disclose expected savings.
