details.key_value: Cost divided by useful life of at least 1 year, minus annual operating-cost savings; no increase for work affecting more than 10 rental units unless cost exceeds $2,000; notice must be within 24 months
details.quote: The landlord shall compute the average cost of the major new improvement(s) per year of useful life by dividing the cost of the completed major new improvement(s) by the number of years of useful life of the improvement(s) provided that the period shall not be less than one (1) year.

details.requirement: The landlord must apportion the monthly improvement increase among affected units by multiplying each tenant's monthly rent by one-twelfth of the annual improvement cost divided by the total monthly rent roll of affected units.
details.key_value: Proportionate to tenant's rent among affected units
details.quote: The amount of the monthly increase which a landlord may charge shall be prorated among all tenants benefiting from the improvements by dividing one-twelfth (1/12th) of the annual cost of the capital improvements by the total monthly rent roll of the units affected by the improvement in the dwelling, occupied or unoccupied, and that product shall be multiplied by the monthly rent paid by each tenant

details.requirement: A tenant is not liable for an improvement surcharge if the tenant receives no benefit; if the tenant benefits, liability cannot exceed the tenant's calculated rent percentage, and the surcharge cannot be charged beyond the improvement's useful life.
details.key_value: No longer than the improvement's useful life
details.quote: No tenant shall be liable for a major new improvement(s) increase if he/she receives no benefit from the improvement nor, if he/she benefits, shall he/she be liable for an increase exceeding the percentage of rent paid by him/her as calculated above, and all such rent increases shall be charged for no period greater than the useful life of the improvements.

details.requirement: The landlord must notify the Board and tenants at least 60 days before the surcharge takes effect and provide specified information to the Board. The Board or a tenant may request a hearing within 30 days of receiving notice. After approval, the landlord must give each tenant one month's prior notice of the effective date.
details.key_value: Board and tenant notice at least 60 days before effect; hearing request within 30 days of notice; tenant notice one month before effect after approval
details.quote: The landlord shall notify the Board and tenants at least sixty (60) days before the effective date of the increase. The notice to the Board shall, on forms provided by the Board, include the amount of increase, a description of the improvement, and the figures used to compute the increase.

details.requirement: A landlord unable to meet reasonable and necessary operating expenses and earn a fair return may apply to the Board for a hardship increase. An increase may be granted only if the dwelling is in substantial compliance and registration requirements are met.
details.quote: To realize a just and reasonable return on the subject property, a landlord may appeal to the Board for a hardship rent increase if the landlord is unable to meet its reasonable and necessary operating expenses and earn a fair rate of return on his investment by submitting a Hardship Increase Application.

details.requirement: The Board must deny an application when inspection or reinspection shows the property is not in substantial compliance. It may conditionally grant an increase on abatement within a reasonable time, not exceeding 45 days.
details.key_value: Abatement period may not exceed 45 days
details.quote: The Board shall deny an application for an increase when a property fails to meet substantial compliance upon completion of an inspection or re-inspection of the property. The Board may conditionally grant the increase subject to the landlord abating the violations within a reasonable time. However, in no event shall this period of time exceed forty-five (45) days.

details.requirement: If violations are not abated within 45 days, the application is denied, the landlord cannot reapply for six months, any conditional increase is revoked, and the landlord must restore collected additional rent by refund or next-month rent deduction.
details.key_value: 45-day abatement deadline; six-month bar on resubmission
details.quote: In the event that such abatement has not taken place within forty-five (45) days, the application will be denied and the landlord will be barred from resubmitting an application for six (6) months. The Board shall revoke any such conditional increase, and the landlord shall be required to restore to the affected tenants all of the additional monies collected pursuant to the increase.

details.requirement: Thirty days before a hardship hearing, the landlord must post conspicuous notices in specified common areas and entrances describing the proposed increase, sample new rent calculation, Rent Increase Factor Table, and tenants' right to testify. Where there is a tenant association, notice must also be hand delivered or sent by certified mail to its president, and the notice must follow specified font and legibility restrictions.
details.key_value: 30 days before the hearing
details.quote: Thirty (30) days before a public hearing on the landlord's application for a hardship increase, the landlord must place conspicuous notices in all common areas, including, but not limited to, all elevators, the first landing of all stairways and staircases, at security and/or receptionist desks, mail rooms and community rooms.

details.requirement: A landlord applying for a hardship increase must submit documented operating, maintenance, repair, vacancy, mortgage, refinancing, and recurring expenses as detailed in the ordinance; vacancies and management costs must be documented and each category may not exceed 5% of gross income. Vacancy loss is allowed only for units cleaned, repaired, and offered on the market within two months. Capital improvements must be itemized with depreciation calculations.
details.key_value: Vacancy and management costs may not each exceed 5% of gross income; vacancy unit must be offered within 2 months
details.quote: The landlord shall submit proof of expenses for operation, maintenance and repairs, including, but not limited to taxes, employees' salaries, all contracted expenses, insurance, fuel, utilities, maintenance and repairs, and reasonable superintendent and/or management fees, as well as expenses for vacancies, which have been held available for rental, to substantiate any hardship increase application.

details.requirement: Attorney's, accountant's, and application fees incurred by a landlord in connection with a Board application may not be included in determining whether the landlord is entitled to a rent increase.
details.quote: No attorney's fees, accountant's fees or application fees incurred by a landlord in connection with any application to the Board shall be included in determining whether a landlord is entitled to any rent increases.

details.requirement: An increase awarded under this section must be apportioned among tenants by dividing the monthly increase by the total monthly rent roll and multiplying that result by each tenant's monthly rent.
details.quote: The monthly increase shall be divided by the total monthly rent roll and that product shall be multiplied by the monthly rent paid by each tenant to establish the amount of increase that each tenant shall be required to pay.

details.requirement: A rental unit may not receive an increase under this section more than once in any 12-month period.
details.key_value: once in any 12-month period
details.quote: No increase pursuant to this Section shall be authorized with respect to a rental unit more than once in any twelve (12) month period

details.requirement: The Board must deny all or part of the requested relief when specific factual findings support the conclusion that the landlord bought the dwelling for an excessive price.
details.quote: The Board shall deny all or a part of the relief requested where specific findings of fact support the conclusion that the landlord purchased the dwelling for an excessive price.

details.requirement: The Board must deny expenses that an efficient operator would not incur.
details.quote: The Board shall also deny any expenses that an efficient operator would not incur.

details.requirement: Either the landlord or tenant may appeal the Board's findings or order on a hardship-increase application to the Superior Court Law Division within 45 days.
details.key_value: 45 days
details.quote: Either the landlord or tenant may appeal the findings or order of the Rent Control Board regarding a hardship increase application to the Law Division of the Superior Court in accordance with New Jersey Court Rules within forty-five (45) days of the findings or order by the Board.

details.requirement: A landlord or agent must keep a copy of the registration form at or adjacent to each dwelling unit, together with a list of vacant units, their most recent vacancy dates, and current and immediately previous rents; these records must be available for inspection during normal business hours by tenants and prospective tenants to whom they pertain.
details.quote: Copies of the registration form shall be kept by the landlord or his/her agent at or adjacent to any dwelling unit as well as a list of any vacant units within such building, of the date on which the unit or units of housing space most recently became vacant, and the current and immediately previous rents of the housing space. These records shall be available for inspection during normal business hours by any tenant or prospective tenant of the housing space to which they pertain.

details.requirement: The Board may deny a rent increase if the landlord fails to register all dwellings with the Rent Control Board.
details.quote: To deny, at its discretion, a rent increase if the landlord fails to register all dwellings with the Rent Control Board.

details.requirement: The Board may grant a rent decrease for a decrease in housing space, services, furniture, furnishings, or equipment; a tenant or group of tenants may petition for one.
details.key_value: A rent decrease may be granted for a decrease in housing space, services, furniture, furnishings, or equipment
details.quote: During the term of this chapter a rent decrease may be granted by the Rent Control Board for any decrease in housing space, services, furniture, furnishings or equipment. A tenant or group of tenants may petition for rent reduction through the Rent Control Board.

details.requirement: For qualifying cessation or inadequate provision of landlord-responsible heat, rent must be decreased by 45% of total rent collected during the service-decrease period.
details.quote:
For the following decreases in services, a petitioner or petitioners rents shall be decreased in accordance with the following percentages of the total rent or rents collected during the period of the decrease in services:
      
      	a.	No heat	45%

details.requirement: For qualifying cessation or inadequate provision of landlord-responsible water service, rent must be decreased by 30% of total rent collected during the service-decrease period.
details.quote:
For the following decreases in services, a petitioner or petitioners rents shall be decreased in accordance with the following percentages of the total rent or rents collected during the period of the decrease in services:
      
      	a.	No heat	45%
      
      	b.	No water	30%

details.requirement: For qualifying absence of landlord-provided hot water, rent must be decreased by 10% to 25% of total rent collected during the service-decrease period.
details.quote: c.	No hot water (When provision of hot water is the responsibility of the landlord)	10-25%

details.requirement: For roof leaks that make the apartment or dwelling unit uninhabitable, rent must be decreased by 25% to 75% of total rent collected during the service-decrease period.
details.quote: d.	Roof leaks (Such as to make the apartment, or dwelling unit uninhabitable)	25-75%

details.requirement: For a nonfunctioning stove or refrigerator supplied by the landlord, rent must be decreased by 10% of total rent collected during the service-decrease period.
details.quote: e.	Nonfunctioning stoves or refrigerators (where supplied by landlord)	10%

details.requirement: For faulty electrical fixtures constituting a dangerous condition or a threat to tenant health and safety, rent must be decreased by 10% to 50% of total rent collected during the service-decrease period.
details.quote: f.	Faulty electrical fixtures (Such as to constitute a dangerous condition, or threat to the health and safety of the tenants) 10-50%

details.requirement: For faulty plumbing, the reduction is 15% per inoperable fixture, capped at 75% of the total rent of all petitioners.
details.key_value: 15% per fixture; maximum 75% of petitioners' total rent
details.quote: g.	Faulty plumbing (Defined as inoperable "fixtures" i.e., tub, sink, toilet, kitchen sink)(15% per fixture, but not to exceed a maximum of 75% of the total rent of all petitioners) 15%

details.requirement: For qualifying elevator inoperability, rent must be decreased by 10% for tenants living on the fifth floor or above in buildings over four stories, when the landlord's neglect caused the inoperability.
details.quote: h.	Inoperable elevator (Shall only apply in buildings over four stories, when inoperability is due to the neglect of the landlord; reduction shall only be applied to tenants of the building living on the fifth floor or above) 10%

details.requirement: When a rent decrease is conditioned on repairs, the landlord may petition for reinstatement of all or part of the reduced rents after completing at least 75% of the ordered repairs; the petition and Board determination must follow the rent-adjustment procedures in § 19:2-13.
details.key_value: At least 75% of ordered repairs completed
details.quote: If a rent decrease is made conditional upon the landlord's performing whatever repairs are deemed necessary to correct a decrease in services, the landlord may petition, upon completion of seventy-five (75%) percent or more of the repairs ordered, for a reinstitution of all or part of the decreased rents.

details.requirement: If the landlord changes the heating service in a way that requires tenants to pay for heat, the Board may grant a rent decrease equal to the cost of providing heat, as determined by the Office of Rent Control.
details.key_value: Decrease equal to the cost of providing heat
details.quote: Where it is found that the landlord has contracted to change the heating service by changing a heating unit or otherwise requiring the tenants to pay for their heat, the Rent Control Board may grant a rent decrease equal to the cost of providing heat as that cost is determined by the Office of Rent Control.

details.requirement: Each party to a hearing may receive assistance in presenting evidence and developing their position from an attorney, legal worker, tenant union representative, or person designated by the party.
details.quote: All parties to a hearing may have assistance in presenting evidence and developing their position from attorneys, legal workers, tenant union representatives or any persons designated by the parties.

details.requirement: A landlord or tenant aggrieved by Board action, regulation, or determination may appeal to the Law Division of the Superior Court under the New Jersey Court Rules within 45 days of the Board action.
details.key_value: 45 days
details.quote: A landlord or tenant aggrieved by any action, regulation or determination of the Board may appeal that action, regulation or determination of the Rent Control Board to the Law Division of the Superior Court in accordance with New Jersey Court Rules within forty-five (45) days of the action taken by the Board.

details.requirement: After the chapter's effective date, a landlord may not charge more than the rent received on that date, except for increases authorized by the chapter.
details.key_value: No more than the rent received on the chapter's effective date, except increases authorized by the chapter
details.quote: No landlord shall after the effective date of this chapter charge any rents in excess of what he/she was receiving from the effective date of this chapter except for increases authorized by this chapter.

details.requirement: On an application supported by credible proof that the preceding 12 months' heating and water expenses, excluding sewer charges, exceed the prior 12 months' expenses by more than 10%, the Administrator must grant the landlord a utilities surcharge.
details.key_value: Expense increase greater than 10%
details.quote: where the landlord substantiates through credible proof to the Rent Control Board Administrator that increases in heating expenses and water expenses (not including sewer charges) for the twelve (12) months immediately preceding his/her application are in excess of ten (10%) percent of the heating expenses and water expenses for the prior twelve (12) months, the Administrator shall grant a utilities surcharge to the applying landlord.

details.requirement: The utilities surcharge may not exceed 15% of the monthly rent roll for buildings with 30 or fewer units, 5% for buildings with more than 30 but fewer than 201 units, or 3% for buildings with more than 200 units. The percentage is calculated against the monthly rent roll in the application month.
details.quote: the increase allowed shall not exceed fifteen (15%) percent of the monthly rent roll of apartments which contain thirty (30) or fewer units; and the increase allowed shall not exceed five (5%) percent of the monthly rent roll of apartments which contain more than thirty (30) units but less than two hundred one (201) units; and, the increase allowed shall not exceed three (3%) percent of the monthly rent roll of apartments which contain more than two hundred (200) units.

details.requirement: After the application date, a finding that heat or water is not provided in accordance with applicable law is a basis to deny a utilities surcharge increase.
details.quote: After the date of application, a finding that heat or water is not provided to the building in conformance with the applicable law shall be a basis for a denial of an increase pursuant to this Section of the rent control ordinance.

details.requirement: If granted, the landlord must calculate each tenant's surcharge by dividing the monthly surcharge by the total rent roll and multiplying the result by the tenant's monthly rent.
details.quote: If the required increase is granted, the landlord shall establish the surcharge to be paid by each tenant by dividing the monthly utilities surcharge granted, by the total rent roll, and then multiplying that product by the monthly rent paid by each tenant.

details.requirement: The landlord must give all tenants written notice of an approved increase at least one month before its effective date and file a copy of the notice with the Administrator.
details.key_value: At least 1 month before effective date
details.quote: The landlord shall notify all tenants in writing of the approved increase. Such notice shall be served upon the tenants at least one (1) month prior to the effective date of the increase. The landlord shall file with the Administrator of the Rent Control Board a copy of the notice that was served upon the tenants.

details.requirement: Periodic or regular base-rent increase limits do not apply to newly constructed multiple dwellings for the shorter of the initial mortgage-loan amortization period or 30 years after construction is completed. The landlord must apply for an exemption certification before occupancy, after receiving a certificate of occupancy, and include a bona fide copy and the unrestricted initial rent. The Board has 30 days to show ineligibility or the exemption is deemed granted; the exemption starts on the first tenant occupancy or 30 days after application, whichever is earlier.
details.key_value: Shorter of initial mortgage amortization period or 30 years after completion
details.quote: The provisions of the Rent Control Ordinance, which limit the periodic or regular increases in base rentals of dwelling units shall not apply to newly constructed multiple dwellings for a period of time not to exceed the period of amortization of any initial mortgage loan obtained for the multiple dwelling, or for thirty (30) years following completion of construction, whichever is less.

details.requirement: If there is no initial mortgage financing, the rent-control exemption lasts 30 years from completion of construction.
details.key_value: 30 years from completion
details.quote: In the event that there is no initial mortgage financing, the period of the exemption from rent control shall be thirty (30) years from the completion of the construction.

details.requirement: A granted exemption remains with the property despite a change in ownership, and the exemption period is not altered.
details.quote: Any exemption from rent control granted pursuant to this Section will remain with the property. Any change in ownership of the property will not affect the exemption.

details.requirement: A dwelling vacant for at least 18 months after the section's effective date, or already vacant on that date, is exempt from rent restrictions for five years if the Board finds rehabilitation costs during a 12-month period exceeded 50% of undepreciated cost or fair market value and the dwelling has a Certificate of Occupancy and meets applicable health and housing codes.
details.key_value: 5-year exemption
details.quote: Dwellings which become vacant after the effective date of this section and remain vacant for a minimum of eighteen (18) months or dwellings which are already vacant on the effective date of this section shall be exempt for a period of five (5) years from any restrictions in the rent that the landlord may charge, if the Rent Control Board determines that the cost of reconstruction or rehabilitation during a twelve (12) month period has exceeded fifty (50%) percent of either the undepreciated cost or the fair market value of the dwelling and that the dwelling has received a Certificate of Occupancy and meets all applicable State and municipal health and housing codes.

details.requirement: An exemption petition must be submitted no later than two years after acquisition of the first City permit for substantial reconstruction or rehabilitation.
details.key_value: No later than 2 years from acquisition of the first permit
details.quote: Petitions for an exemption under this section, whether filed with a Certificate of Occupancy or a Temporary Certificate of Occupancy, shall be submitted no later than two (2) years from the date of the acquisition of the first permit from the City of Newark for the substantial reconstruction or rehabilitation.

details.requirement: An applicant may request a hearing before the Rent Control Board from the Administrator's decision.
details.quote: An applicant may file a request for a hearing before the Rent Control Board from the decision of the Administrator.

details.requirement: At least 90 days before the five-year exemption expires, the landlord must notify tenants and the Rent Control Board that rent restrictions will apply when the exemption ends.
details.key_value: At least 90 days before expiration
details.quote: At least ninety (90) days prior to the expiration of the five (5) year exemption from rent control, the landlord shall notify the tenants and the Rent Control Board that the tenancy shall be subject to rent charge restrictions upon the expiration of the exemption period.

details.requirement: A substantially reconstructed or rehabilitated dwelling may charge an unrestricted initial rent if the Board determines that rehabilitation costs in a 12-month period exceed 50% of fair market value, the work complies with the Uniform Construction Code, and the required occupancy certificate confirms conformity with the submitted plan and applicable codes. The Board must consider an Engineering Department inspection and disallow normal-maintenance costs. Rehabilitation must be complete before application; the petition must be filed within two years of the first permit and state the unrestricted initial rent. The application is subject to acceptance and tenant-notice procedures.
details.key_value: Unrestricted initial rent
details.quote: Dwellings which are substantially reconstructed or rehabilitated shall not be restricted in regard to the initial rent charged if the Rent Control Board has made the following determinations:

details.requirement: For an unrestricted rental increase approved by the Board, the petitioner must give each tenant one month's prior notice of its effective date.
details.key_value: 1 month before effective date
details.quote: the petitioner shall give each tenant one (1) month prior notice of the effective date of any unrestricted rental increase approved by the Rent Control Board.

details.requirement: A landlord who rehabilitates a vacant apartment unit by spending at least 12 months of actual monthly rent per unit is entitled to a maximum 10% increase in actual monthly rent.
details.key_value: Maximum 10%
details.quote: Any landlord that rehabilitates a vacant apartment unit by spending a total amount equal to at least twelve (12) months of actual monthly rent per unit will be entitled to a maximum of ten percent (10%) increase in the actual monthly rent.

details.requirement: The landlord must post notice of a rent-increase application in a conspicuous place in the apartment building on the date of application.
details.key_value: On the date of application
details.quote: A notice of any application for a rent increase under this section shall be posted in a conspicuous place in the apartment building by the landlord on the date of the application.

details.requirement: Only one increase may be granted under this section for the same apartment unit in any twelve-month period.
details.key_value: One increase per unit in any 12-month period
details.quote: The landlord may be granted only one (1) increase under this section for the same apartment unit in any twelve (12) month period.

details.requirement: Qualifying purchasers of City-owned dwellings are exempt from rent restrictions for five years, subject to the stated vacancy, rehabilitation, and code-compliance requirements.
details.key_value: Five years
details.quote: person(s), who acquire City-owned dwellings (if the dwellings are not substandard multiple dwelling or newly constructed multiple dwelling) in the City of Newark shall be exempted for a period of five (5) years from any restrictions in the rent that the landlord may charge provided that:

details.requirement: Rent for covered housing space and services is controlled at the rent received on September 4, 1985, and increases are prohibited except as provided in the chapter.
details.key_value: Rent level received on September 4, 1985
details.quote: All rent for the rental of housing space and services in dwellings to which this chapter is applicable are hereby controlled at the rent level received by the landlord, as of the first date that this chapter was adopted, on September 4, 1985, and no rental increases shall hereafter be instituted, except as provided in this chapter as amended and supplemented.

details.requirement: The Rent Control Board must not grant increases exceeding 25 percent in any one year for any tenant.
details.key_value: 25% in any one year
details.quote: the Rent Control Board shall not grant increases exceeding twenty-five (25%) percent in any one (1) year for any tenant.

details.requirement: In determining whether an increase exceeds 25 percent, increases under Sections 19:2-3, 19:2-7, and 19:2-8 during the preceding twelve months must be added together.
details.key_value: Add covered increases occurring within the prior 12 months
details.quote: all increases pursuant to Section 19:2-3, Rent Increases, 19:2-7, Major New Improvements and 19:2-8, Landlord Hardships, occurring within twelve (12) months prior to the effective date of the increase shall be added to determine if that amount exceeds twenty-five (25%) percent of the prior monthly rent.

details.requirement: Before entering into a lease for premises in an exempt multiple dwelling, the owner must give prospective tenants a written statement that the dwelling is exempt and for how long the exemption remains.
details.quote: shall, prior to entering into any lease with a person(s) for tenancy of any premises located in the multiple dwelling, furnish the prospective tenant(s) with a written statement that the multiple dwelling in which the premises is located is exempt from rent control or rent leveling for such time as may remain in the exemption period.

details.requirement: Each lease offered for a dwelling unit in an exempt multiple dwelling during the exemption period must include a provision notifying the tenant of the exemption.
details.quote: Each lease offered to a prospective tenant(s) for any dwelling unit therein during the period the multiple dwelling is so exempted shall contain a provision notifying the tenant(s) of the exemption.

details.requirement: At least 30 days before the exemption ends, the owner must file notice of the termination date with the Municipal Construction Official and Office of Rent Control.
details.key_value: At least 30 days before termination
details.quote: The owner shall, at least thirty (30) days prior to the date of the termination of the exemption period afforded pursuant to this chapter, file with the Municipal Construction Official and the Office of Rent Control a notice of the date of termination of the exemption period for the affected multiple dwelling.

tenant_conditions: When determining whether the 25% limit is exceeded, increases under §§ 19:2-3, 19:2-7, and 19:2-8 within 12 months before the increase's effective date are combined.
key_value: 25% in any one-year period

details.requirement: At lease expiration or termination of a periodic tenancy, a landlord may not request or receive an increase exceeding the CPI increase calculated using the specified 15-month and 3-month reference points, and the increase may never exceed 4%.
details.key_value: The increase is limited to the CPI increase measured from 15 months before the proposed increase to 3 months before it, and may not exceed 4%.
details.quote: At the expiration of a lease or at the termination of the lease of a periodic tenant, no landlord may request or receive an increase greater than the percentage increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) from the CPI fifteen (15) months prior to the month of the proposed rent increase to the CPI three (3) months prior to the month of the proposed rent increase. In no case shall the allowable rent increase exceed four (4%) percent.

details.requirement: Rent for a housing space may not be increased beyond the permitted percentage in any consecutive twelve-month period, regardless of tenant changes, ownership changes, or vacancy.
details.key_value: No more than the permitted percentage increase in any consecutive 12-month period.
details.quote: The rents for any housing space shall not be increased more than the percentages stated above in any consecutive twelve (12) month period irrespective of the number of different tenants occupying the housing space during the twelve (12) month period, any change of ownership of the landlord or vacancy of the housing space.

details.requirement: A tenant may challenge the legality of the rent charged immediately before an authorized increase.
details.quote: This provision does not preclude a tenant from challenging the legality of the rent being charged immediately prior to an increase authorized by this section.

details.requirement: The landlord must report and register all on-site parking fees with the Rent Control Board, and parking fees are covered by the rent-control ordinance.
details.quote: The landlord shall report and register all on-site parking fees with the Rent Control Board. Parking fees should be specifically included as being covered under all provisions of the rent control ordinance.

details.requirement: No annual rent increase, major new improvement surcharge, tax surcharge, or hardship increase is allowed if the dwelling is not in substantial compliance or registration requirements have not been met.
details.quote: No annual rent increase, major new improvement surcharge, tax surcharge, or hardship increase is allowed, if the dwelling is not in substantial compliance and/or has not met registration requirements as specified in subsection 19:2-9.8.

details.requirement: The landlord must credit the tenant for excess rent collected over a period not exceeding fourteen months, or refund the excess within one month if the tenant is no longer in occupancy.
details.key_value: Credit over a period not exceeding 14 months; if the tenant is no longer in occupancy, refund within 1 month.
details.quote: The landlord shall rebate to the tenant any amount of rent collected in excess of that permissible pursuant to the terms of this chapter by crediting the tenant with the amount of excess rent paid over a period not to exceed fourteen (14) months, or in the event the tenant is no longer in occupancy, by refunding within a one (1) month period.

details.requirement: A tax surcharge may not exceed the tenant's allocated share calculated by dividing one-twelfth of the annual municipal property-tax increase by the total monthly rent roll, then multiplying that result by the tenant's monthly rent; the tenant's liability is capped at the tenant's percentage of the entire rent roll.
details.key_value: One-twelfth of the annual property-tax increase divided by the total monthly rent roll and multiplied by the tenant's monthly rent; liability cannot exceed the tenant's percentage of the entire rent roll.
details.quote: The landlord shall divide one-twelfth (1/12th) of the annual increase in the present property tax over the property tax of the previous year by the total monthly rent roll, and that product shall be multiplied by the monthly rent paid by each tenant to establish the amount of surcharge that each tenant shall be required to pay. The tenant shall not be liable for a tax surcharge exceeding the tenant's percentage of the entire rent roll for the dwelling.

details.requirement: A landlord seeking a tax surcharge must petition the Board and give the tenant and Board at least 30 days' advance notice of the increase and the listed surcharge calculations and supporting figures.
details.key_value: At least 30 days before the proposed increase.
details.quote: Any landlord seeking a surcharge shall petition the Board for approval and shall give notice to the tenant and the Board, at least thirty (30) days prior to the increase sought, of the calculations involved in computing the tax surcharge, including the present property tax for the dwelling; the property tax for the dwelling for the previous year; total rent rolls of all units, occupied or unoccupied in the dwelling; the percentage of the increase over the total rent roll; the rent of the tenant; and the percentage of his/her present rent compared to the total rent roll.

details.requirement: The tenant's tax surcharge must be paid in equal monthly installments and only after the landlord gives the statutory one-month advance notice.
details.key_value: Equal monthly payments; one-month advance notice.
details.quote: The tax surcharge each tenant is liable for shall be paid in equal monthly payments only after the landlord gives the tenant one (1) month prior notice of the increase as required by statute.

details.requirement: A party dissatisfied with the Board's tax-surcharge ruling may appeal to the Superior Court Law Division or Municipal Council within 45 days; a party dissatisfied with the Council's decision may appeal to the Law Division.
details.key_value: 45 days from the Board's ruling to appeal to the Superior Court Law Division or Municipal Council.
details.quote: Any party dissatisfied with the ruling of the Rent Control Board on a Tax Surcharge Application may appeal the matter to either the Law Division of the Superior Court in accordance with New Jersey Court Rules or the Municipal Council by filing a notice of appeal with the City Clerk within forty-five (45) days of the Board's ruling.  Any party dissatisfied with the decision by the Municipal Council may appeal the matter to the Law Division of the Superior Court in accordance with New Jersey Court Rules.

details.requirement: Tenants are entitled to a tax decrease if municipal property taxes are reduced by a lower tax rate or assessment, apportioned in the same manner as tax surcharges.
details.key_value: Apportioned in the same manner as a tax surcharge under subsection 19:2-5.1.
details.quote: If the municipal property taxes are decreased in a given year due to either a decrease in the property tax rate or a lowering of the assessed evaluation of the property by the municipality, then the tenants are entitled to a tax decrease. Apportionment of such decrease shall be in the same manner as apportionment of tax surcharge under subsection 19:2-5.1.

details.requirement: When the landlord succeeds in a tax appeal and taxes are reduced, the tenant must receive 75% of the reduction attributable to the tenant's tax portion after reasonable appeal expenses are deducted.
details.key_value: 75% of the reduction applied to the tenant's tax portion, after reasonable appeal expenses.
details.quote: In the event a tax appeal is taken by the landlord and the landlord is successful in the appeal and the taxes reduced, the tenant shall receive seventy-five (75%) percent of the reductions as applied to its tax portion, after deducting all reasonable expenses incurred by the landlord in prosecuting the appeal.

details.requirement: The landlord must notify tenants within 30 days of receiving a tax rebate of the amount received and the tenant's calculation, and must forward the amount due within that same 30-day period.
details.key_value: Within 30 days after the landlord receives the rebate; payment is due in the same 30-day period.
details.quote: The landlord must notify the tenants within thirty (30) days of the time the landlord receives his/her rebate of the amount he/she has received with the computations on how much the tenant is entitled to. The amount due the tenant shall be forwarded to the tenant within the same thirty (30) day period.

details.requirement: A landlord seeking a major-new-improvement surcharge must calculate the annual cost by dividing the completed improvement cost by its useful life (at least one year), subtract annual savings in operating costs, and disclose all expected savings; the landlord bears the burden of proving useful life.
details.key_value: Useful life cannot be less than one year; annual operating-cost savings must be subtracted.
details.quote: The landlord shall compute the average cost of the major new improvement(s) per year of useful life by dividing the cost of the completed major new improvement(s) by the number of years of useful life of the improvement(s) provided that the period shall not be less than one (1) year. The useful life is the actual number of years that the major improvement(s) is expected to last before needing replacement. The burden of proof is on the landlord to establish the useful life of the improvement(s). If the major new improvement(s) lowers the landlord's operating costs, the annual cost savings must be subtracted from the annual major new improvement(s) surcharge. The landlord is required to disclose all expected cost savings that will result from the major new improvement(s).

details.requirement: No surcharge is permitted for improvements affecting more than ten rental units unless the total cost exceeds $2,000, or for improvements completed more than 24 months before the landlord notifies the Board.
details.key_value: More than 10 rental units requires total cost over $2,000; improvement must not have been completed more than 24 months before notice to the Board.
details.quote: No increase shall be permitted for major new improvement(s) affecting more than ten (10) rental units, unless the total cost thereof exceeds two thousand ($2.000.00) dollars. No increase shall be permitted for major new improvement(s) completed more than twenty-four (24) months prior to the date upon which notice to the Board of the improvements has been provided by the landlord.

details.requirement: A major-new-improvement rent increase may not be granted if the dwelling is not in substantial compliance or the landlord has not met registration requirements.
details.quote: In no case will a major new improvement(s) rent increase be granted if the dwelling is not in substantial compliance and/or if the landlord has not met the registration requirements as specified in subsection 19:1-10.

details.requirement: The monthly improvement increase must be apportioned among benefiting tenants by dividing one-twelfth of annual improvement cost by the total monthly rent roll of affected units and multiplying by each tenant's monthly rent.
details.key_value: One-twelfth of annual improvement cost divided by the affected units' total monthly rent roll, multiplied by the tenant's monthly rent.
details.quote: The amount of the monthly increase which a landlord may charge shall be prorated among all tenants benefiting from the improvements by dividing one-twelfth (1/12th) of the annual cost of the capital improvements by the total monthly rent roll of the units affected by the improvement in the dwelling, occupied or unoccupied, and that product shall be multiplied by the monthly rent paid by each tenant to establish the amount of capital improvement increase that each tenant shall be required to pay.

details.requirement: A tenant owes no improvement surcharge without benefiting from the improvement; a benefiting tenant cannot be charged more than the calculated rent share, and the surcharge cannot continue beyond the improvement's useful life.
details.key_value: No liability without benefit; otherwise capped at the tenant's calculated rent share and limited to the useful life.
details.quote: No tenant shall be liable for a major new improvement(s) increase if he/she receives no benefit from the improvement nor, if he/she benefits, shall he/she be liable for an increase exceeding the percentage of rent paid by him/her as calculated above, and all such rent increases shall be charged for no period greater than the useful life of the improvements.

details.requirement: The landlord must notify the Board and tenants at least 60 days before the increase takes effect, including the amount, improvement description, and calculations. The Board or a tenant may request a hearing within 30 days after receiving notice.
details.key_value: Notice at least 60 days before the effective date; hearing request within 30 days of receipt.
details.quote: The landlord shall notify the Board and tenants at least sixty (60) days before the effective date of the increase. The notice to the Board shall, on forms provided by the Board, include the amount of increase, a description of the improvement, and the figures used to compute the increase. The Board or a tenant may request a hearing within thirty (30) days of receipt of notice from the landlord.

details.requirement: After Board approval of a major-new-improvement surcharge, the landlord must give each tenant one month's prior notice of its effective date.
details.key_value: One month prior notice.
details.quote: After approval by the Board of a major new improvement surcharge, the landlord shall give to each tenant one (1) month prior notice of the effective date of the major new improvement surcharge as required by statute.

details.requirement: A landlord or tenant may appeal a Board finding or order on a major-improvement application to the Superior Court Law Division or Municipal Council within 45 days; a party dissatisfied with the Council decision may appeal to the Law Division.
details.key_value: 45 days from the Board's findings or order.
details.quote: Either landlord or tenant may appeal the findings or order of the Rent Control Board regarding a major new improvement application to either the Law Division of the Superior Court in accordance with New Jersey Court Rules or the Municipal Council by filing a notice of appeal with the City Clerk within forty-five (45) days of the findings or order of the Board.  Either party dissatisfied with the decision by the Municipal Council may appeal the matter to the Law Division of the Superior Court in accordance with New Jersey Court Rules.

details.requirement: A landlord unable to meet reasonable and necessary operating expenses and earn a fair return may apply to the Board for a hardship rent increase; an application may be granted only if the dwelling is in substantial compliance and registration requirements are met.
details.quote: To realize a just and reasonable return on the subject property, a landlord may appeal to the Board for a hardship rent increase if the landlord is unable to meet its reasonable and necessary operating expenses and earn a fair rate of return on his investment by submitting a Hardship Increase Application. The Board will hold a public hearing on the application following the procedure outlined in 19:2-13. Inspections of the dwelling must take place before a hearing. A re-inspection may take place after the hearing as detailed in this section. An application will be granted only if the dwelling meets the definition of substantial compliance and the landlord has met the registration requirements specified in this chapter.

details.requirement: If violations are not abated within 45 days, the hardship application must be denied, the landlord is barred from reapplying for six months, any conditional increase must be revoked, and the landlord must return the additional amounts collected by refund or rent deduction.
details.key_value: Abatement within 45 days; six-month reapplication bar; collected increase restored by refund or next-month rent deduction.
details.quote: In the event that such abatement has not taken place within forty-five (45) days, the application will be denied and the landlord will be barred from resubmitting an application for six (6) months. The Board shall revoke any such conditional increase, and the landlord shall be required to restore to the affected tenants all of the additional monies collected pursuant to the increase. The restoration of monies shall be in the form of either a direct refund of all monies collected or a deduction from the next month's rent.

details.requirement: At least 30 days before the hardship hearing, the landlord must post notices in specified common areas and building locations with the proposed increase, sample rent calculation, Rent Increase Factor Table, and tenant testimony rights; where a tenant association exists, notice must be hand-delivered or sent by certified mail to its president. The notice must meet the specified font and format rules.
details.key_value: 30 days before the public hearing.
details.quote: Thirty (30) days before a public hearing on the landlord's application for a hardship increase, the landlord must place conspicuous notices in all common areas, including, but not limited to, all elevators, the first landing of all stairways and staircases, at security and/or receptionist desks, mail rooms and community rooms. Notices shall also be placed at the entrance(s) of: the building, laundry rooms, gym rooms, recreation rooms and meeting rooms. The notice must detail the proposed percentage increase in rent, a sample calculation of a new rent amount based on the percentage increase, the Rent Increase Factor Table, and the right of tenants and tenant associations to testify against the application as enumerated in Section 19:2-13.

details.requirement: Vacancy and management expenses must be fully documented and may not exceed 5% of the landlord's gross income in either category. Vacancy loss is allowed only for units cleaned, repaired, and offered on the market within two months, with supporting proof.
details.key_value: Each category may not exceed 5% of gross income; vacancy units must be cleaned, repaired, and offered within two months.
details.quote: Amounts allowed for vacancies and for management costs shall be fully documented, and in no event shall allowable expenses in either category exceed five (5%) percent of the landlord's gross income. Management costs shall include all administrative and supervisory costs. The Board shall only allow a vacancy loss for housing spaces that are cleaned, repaired, and offered on the market within two months. Landlord must submit proofs of the same in the form of receipts, contracts, advertisements and lease offers.

details.requirement: Attorney, accountant, and application fees incurred by a landlord in connection with a Board application may not be included in determining entitlement to a rent increase.
details.quote: No attorney's fees, accountant's fees or application fees incurred by a landlord in connection with any application to the Board shall be included in determining whether a landlord is entitled to any rent increases.

details.requirement: A hardship increase awarded by the Board must be apportioned by dividing the monthly increase by the total monthly rent roll and multiplying by each tenant's monthly rent.
details.key_value: Monthly increase divided by total monthly rent roll, multiplied by each tenant's monthly rent.
details.quote: The monthly increase shall be divided by the total monthly rent roll and that product shall be multiplied by the monthly rent paid by each tenant to establish the amount of increase that each tenant shall be required to pay.

details.requirement: A rental unit may not receive a hardship increase more than once in any 12-month period, and the Board may not hold a hearing on such an application more than once in that period.
details.key_value: No more than once in any 12-month period.
details.quote: No increase pursuant to this section shall be authorized with respect to a rental unit more than once in any twelve (12) month period, nor shall the Board conduct a hearing with respect to an application for such a rent increase for a rental unit more than once within a twelve (12) month period.

details.requirement: The Board must deny all or part of requested hardship relief when supported findings show the landlord purchased the dwelling at an excessive price, and must deny expenses an efficient operator would not incur; the Board may require specified prior-owner or inspection information.
details.quote: The Board shall deny all or a part of the relief requested where specific findings of fact support the conclusion that the landlord purchased the dwelling for an excessive price.  Excessive purchase price is hereby defined as the purchase price such that at the time of purchase a reasonable investor could not expect to earn a fair return upon his/her investment. The Board shall also deny any expenses that an efficient operator would not incur.  The Board, in its discretion, may require the landlord provide any information he received from the prior owner or from his own inspection regarding the income and expenses of the property and the physical condition of the property prior to the purchase.

details.requirement: Either the landlord or tenant may appeal a Rent Control Board finding or order on a hardship increase application to the Law Division of the Superior Court or the Municipal Council by filing a notice of appeal with the City Clerk within 45 days. A party dissatisfied with the Council's decision may appeal to the Law Division.
details.key_value: 45 days
details.quote: Either landlord or tenant may appeal the findings or order of the Rent Control Board regarding a hardship increase application to either the Law Division of the Superior Court in accordance with New Jersey Court Rules or the Municipal Council by filing a notice of appeal with the City Clerk within forty-five (45) days of the findings or order by the Board.

details.requirement: The landlord or agent must keep registration forms at or adjacent to the dwelling and keep a list of vacant units, their most recent vacancy dates, and current and immediately previous rents. The records must be available for inspection during normal business hours by a tenant or prospective tenant of the relevant housing space.
details.quote: Copies of the registration form shall be kept by the landlord or his/her agent at or adjacent to any dwelling unit as well as a list of any vacant units within such building, of the date on which the unit or units of housing space most recently became vacant, and the current and immediately previous rents of the housing space.

details.requirement: A tenant or group of tenants may petition the Rent Control Board for a rent reduction when housing space, services, furniture, furnishings, or equipment decreases; the Board may grant a decrease.
details.key_value: Rent decrease may be granted for any decrease in housing space, services, furniture, furnishings or equipment
details.quote: During the term of this chapter a rent decrease may be granted by the Rent Control Board for any decrease in housing space, services, furniture, furnishings or equipment. A tenant or group of tenants may petition for rent reduction through the Rent Control Board.

details.requirement: For a qualifying decrease in services due to no heat, the rent must be decreased by 45% of total rent collected during the period of the service decrease.
details.quote:
For the following decreases in services, a petitioner or petitioners rents shall be decreased in accordance with the following percentages of the total rent or rents collected during the period of the decrease in services:
	a.	No heat	45%

details.requirement: For a qualifying decrease in services due to no water, the rent must be decreased by 30% of total rent collected during the period of the service decrease.
details.quote:
For the following decreases in services, a petitioner or petitioners rents shall be decreased in accordance with the following percentages of the total rent or rents collected during the period of the decrease in services:
	a.	No heat	45%
	b.	No water	30%

details.requirement: For qualifying lack of hot water, the rent must be decreased by 10% to 25% of total rent collected during the service decrease when the landlord is responsible for providing hot water.

details.requirement: If the landlord has completed at least 75% of repairs required by a conditional rent decrease, the landlord may petition for reinstatement of all or part of the decreased rent.
details.key_value: 75% or more of ordered repairs completed
details.quote: upon completion of seventy-five (75%) percent or more of the repairs ordered, for a reinstitution of all or part of the decreased rents.

details.requirement: The Board may grant a rent decrease equal to the cost of providing heat when the landlord changes the heating service so tenants must pay for heat.
details.key_value: Decrease equal to the cost of providing heat
details.quote: Where it is found that the landlord has contracted to change the heating service by changing a heating unit or otherwise requiring the tenants to pay for their heat, the Rent Control Board may grant a rent decrease equal to the cost of providing heat

details.requirement: A party to a hearing may receive assistance in presenting evidence and developing their position from a designated person, including an attorney or tenant union representative.
details.quote: All parties to a hearing may have assistance in presenting evidence and developing their position from attorneys, legal workers, tenant union representatives or any persons designated by the parties.

details.requirement: A landlord or tenant aggrieved by Board action may appeal to the Superior Court Law Division or Municipal Council by filing a notice with the City Clerk within 45 days; a party dissatisfied with the Council's decision may appeal to the Law Division.
details.key_value: 45 days from Board action
details.quote: A landlord or tenant aggrieved by any action, regulation or determination of the Board may appeal that action, regulation or determination of the Rent Control Board to either the Law Division of the Superior Court in accordance with New Jersey Court Rules or the Municipal Council by filing a notice of appeal with the City Clerk within forty-five (45) days of the action taken by the Board.

details.requirement: A landlord may not charge more than the rent received on the chapter's effective date except for increases authorized by the chapter.
details.key_value: Rent received on the effective date of the chapter, except authorized increases
details.quote: No landlord shall after the effective date of this chapter charge any rents in excess of what he/she was receiving from the effective date of this chapter except for increases authorized by this chapter.

details.requirement: If the landlord substantiates that heating and water expenses (excluding sewer charges) for the preceding 12 months increased by more than 10% over the prior 12 months, the Administrator must grant a utilities surcharge. The permitted surcharge is capped by the building's unit count.
details.key_value: Maximum surcharge: 15%, 5%, or 3% of the monthly rent roll depending on unit count
details.quote: where the landlord substantiates through credible proof to the Rent Control Board Administrator that increases in heating expenses and water expenses (not including sewer charges) for the twelve (12) months immediately preceding his/her application are in excess of ten (10%) percent of the heating expenses and water expenses for the prior twelve (12) months, the Administrator shall grant a utilities surcharge to the applying landlord.

details.requirement: A finding after the application date that the building is not provided heat or water in compliance with applicable law is grounds to deny a utilities surcharge increase.
details.quote: After the date of application, a finding that heat or water is not provided to the building in conformance with the applicable law shall be a basis for a denial of an increase pursuant to this section of the rent control ordinance.

details.requirement: If a surcharge is granted, the landlord must allocate it to each tenant by dividing the monthly surcharge by the total rent roll and multiplying the result by that tenant's monthly rent.
details.quote: the landlord shall establish the surcharge to be paid by each tenant by dividing the monthly utilities surcharge granted, by the total rent roll, and then multiplying that product by the monthly rent paid by each tenant.

details.requirement: The landlord must give all tenants written notice of an approved increase at least one month before it takes effect and file a copy with the Administrator.
details.key_value: At least one month before the increase takes effect
details.quote: The landlord shall notify all tenants in writing of the approved increase. Such notice shall be served upon the tenants at least one (1) month prior to the effective date of the increase. The landlord shall file with the Administrator of the Rent Control Board a copy of the notice

details.requirement: Qualifying newly constructed multiple dwellings are exempt from restrictions on periodic or regular base-rent increases for no longer than the initial mortgage amortization period or 30 years after completion, whichever is shorter. Without initial mortgage financing, the exemption lasts 30 years after completion.
details.key_value: Mortgage amortization period or 30 years after completion, whichever is shorter; 30 years without initial mortgage financing
details.quote: The provisions of the Rent Control Ordinance, which limit the periodic or regular increases in base rentals of dwelling units shall not apply to newly constructed multiple dwellings for a period of time not to exceed the period of amortization of any initial mortgage loan obtained for the multiple dwelling, or for thirty (30) years following completion of construction, whichever is less.

details.requirement: Qualifying vacant dwellings receive a five-year exemption from rent restrictions if the Board finds qualifying rehabilitation costs and the dwelling has a Certificate of Occupancy and meets applicable health and housing codes.
details.key_value: 5 years
details.quote: Dwellings which become vacant after the effective date of this section and remain vacant for a minimum of eighteen (18) months or dwellings which are already vacant on the effective date of this section shall be exempt for a period of five (5) years from any restrictions in the rent that the landlord may charge

details.requirement: At least 90 days before the five-year exemption expires, the landlord must notify tenants and the Board that rent restrictions will apply when the exemption ends.
details.key_value: At least 90 days before the exemption expires
details.quote: At least ninety (90) days prior to the expiration of the five (5) year exemption from rent control, the landlord shall notify the tenants and the Rent Control Board that the tenancy shall be subject to rent charge restrictions upon the expiration of the exemption period.

details.requirement: A substantially reconstructed or rehabilitated dwelling's initial rent is unrestricted only after Board determinations that rehabilitation costs exceed 50% of fair market value, work meets construction-code requirements, required permits and documentation are provided, a qualifying Certificate of Occupancy is issued, ordinary maintenance costs are excluded, and the other application requirements are met.
details.key_value: Initial rent is unrestricted if the specified determinations and application requirements are met
details.quote: Dwellings which are substantially reconstructed or rehabilitated shall not be restricted in regard to the initial rent charged if the Rent Control Board has made the following determinations:

details.requirement: A landlord who rehabilitates a vacant apartment unit by spending at least 12 months of actual monthly rent per unit may receive an increase of no more than 10% of actual monthly rent.
details.key_value: Maximum 10% increase
details.quote: Any landlord that rehabilitates a vacant apartment unit by spending a total amount equal to at least twelve (12) months of actual monthly rent per unit will be entitled to a maximum of ten percent (10%)  increase in the actual monthly rent.

details.requirement: The landlord must post notice of a rent-increase application in a conspicuous place in the building on the application date.
details.key_value: On the application date
details.quote: A notice of any application for a rent increase under this section shall be posted in a conspicuous place in the apartment building by the landlord on the date of the application.

details.requirement: A landlord may receive no more than one increase under this section for the same apartment unit in any 12-month period.
details.key_value: One increase per unit in any 12-month period
details.quote: The landlord may be granted only one (1) increase under this section for the same apartment unit in any twelve (12) month period.

details.requirement: Rent for covered housing space and services is controlled at the level received on September 4, 1985; no later rent increase may be instituted except as provided by the chapter.
details.key_value: Rent received on September 4, 1985, except increases authorized by the chapter
details.quote: All rent for the rental of housing space and services in dwellings to which this chapter is applicable are hereby controlled at the rent level received by the landlord, as of the first date that this chapter was adopted, on September 4, 1985, and no rental increases shall hereafter be instituted, except as provided in this chapter as amended and supplemented.

details.requirement: Before entering a lease for premises in a multiple dwelling exempt from rent control or rent leveling, the owner must provide prospective tenants a written exemption statement, and every lease offered during the exemption must disclose the exemption.
details.key_value: Before entering the lease; exemption provision in each lease offered during the exemption period
details.quote: The owner of any multiple dwelling exempted from a rent control or rent leveling ordinance pursuant to this chapter, shall, prior to entering into any lease with a person(s) for tenancy of any premises located in the multiple dwelling, furnish the prospective tenant(s) with a written statement that the multiple dwelling in which the premises is located is exempt from rent control or rent leveling for such time as may remain in the exemption period.
